body.cap: NUCODE’s ultra-low-power IoT communication modules and development boards integrated with external devices and modules. The modular expansion architecture supports a wide range of IoT device development and testing environments. | Source – NUCODE

body.x: As artificial intelligence (AI) technologies continue to advance, the Internet of Things (IoT) is once again gaining strategic importance. By enabling sensors and devices to exchange data through network connectivity, IoT has become a core technology across smart cities, healthcare, industrial safety, and security. However, the global IoT market remains heavily dependent on communication modules sourced from specific regions, raising persistent concerns around technical support limitations, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and supply chain risks. As a result, demand is growing for more stable, flexible, and accessible IoT development environments.

NUCODE (CEO Bruce Lee) was founded to address these challenges. Centered on its ultra-low-power IoT communication modules, branded as the “NU Module,” and its integrated development environment, “NU-Works,” the company offers a modular development platform designed to make IoT product and service development significantly more accessible. Leveraging this technology, NUCODE plans to showcase its solutions to the global market at CES 2026.

NUCODE develops and manufactures ultra-compact, ultra-low-power IoT communication modules based on Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and Wi-Fi. Operating in unlicensed frequency bands including 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz, the modules are optimized for battery-powered devices and environments with limited power availability. According to the company, the modules achieve superior power efficiency compared to competing products under similar conditions, making them well-suited for IoT devices that require long-term operation.

A key differentiator of NUCODE’s approach lies in the dual-purpose design of its modules. Unlike conventional IoT development processes—where development kits, prototype boards, and mass-production components are typically separate—NUCODE’s modules are designed to support hardware integration, wireless communication, testing, and mass production within a single form factor. This unified approach reduces both initial development costs and reliance on specialized equipment.

body.cap: Prototype of NUCODE’s ultra-low-power IoT communication module. Featuring a compact BLE-based design, the module is suitable for both development and mass production. | Photo – AVING News

body.x: In addition, NUCODE provides its proprietary development environment, NU-Works, which helps users understand hardware design flows and communication structures even without deep technical expertise. By combining hardware modules with an integrated development platform, NUCODE aims to significantly lower the entry barrier to hardware and IoT development.

This strategy was further validated during the “:BUILD Physical AI Vibe Coding Hackathon 2025 (1st Edition),” held in late September. The hackathon, themed “Bluetooth Remote Control Ideas through Vibe Coding,” was conducted in collaboration with global technology companies and organizations including Glimpse, AskItMore, Nordic Semiconductor, TE Connectivity, and Geekble.

During the event, each team was provided with two NU40 DK units (based on the nRF52840 development platform) and personal smartphones. Participants successfully implemented Bluetooth-based remote control applications within a single day. Notably, more than half of the participants were non-developers—such as students, designers, planners, and marketers—yet every team achieved full functionality, including LED control and mobile app integration.

body.cap: NUCODE’s NU40 DK development board, designed for Bluetooth remote control and device integration testing. | Photo – AVING News

body.x: NUCODE explained that the hackathon went beyond software-focused coding exercises, offering participants hands-on experience with end-to-end development connecting hardware, wireless communication, and applications. This represents a practical extension of the emerging “vibe coding” trend into real-world IoT and physical AI environments.

Today, NUCODE’s technology is being applied across a wide range of use cases, including construction site safety SOS buttons, medical biometric monitoring devices, vehicle and maritime safety equipment, smart city sensors, and security CCTV pilot projects. Several customers using NUCODE modules have demonstrated their technological competitiveness through international exhibitions and public-sector deployments.

Security and supply chain resilience have also become key factors driving global interest in NUCODE. The global IoT market’s heavy reliance on cost-competitive modules from a limited number of regions has intensified concerns over geopolitical risks, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and potential supply disruptions. In sensitive sectors such as smart homes, industrial sensors, and security systems, module-level reliability and source code controllability are increasingly critical decision criteria.

Against this backdrop, NUCODE positions its internally designed and developed ultra-low-power IoT modules as a compelling alternative. The company emphasizes full source code control and the ability to tailor designs to meet region- and market-specific security requirements. This approach offers global enterprises and system integrators (SIs) a viable option to diversify supply chains while addressing both security and operational stability.

body.cap: Overview of Nordic Semiconductor’s booth at CES 2025. Nordic is expanding its ecosystem with global partners, centered on next-generation ultra-low-power wireless solutions. | Source – Nordic Semiconductor

body.x: Notably, NUCODE maintains a strategic partnership with Nordic Semiconductor, a global leader in low-power Bluetooth and wireless technologies. At CES 2026, NUCODE will showcase its solutions as a partner exhibitor within Nordic Semiconductor’s booth—an indication of the technical credibility and ecosystem alignment it has achieved within the global semiconductor industry.

Bruce Lee, CEO of NUCODE, stated, “CES 2026 will be a critical stage for validating NUCODE’s technology in the global market. In the era of Physical AI, where AI connects directly to the physical world, our goal is to grow into a foundational ultra-low-power IoT infrastructure company that reliably links devices and communications.”

Meanwhile, Nordic Semiconductor will participate in CES 2026, held from January 6 to 9 in Las Vegas, USA, where it will unveil a broad portfolio of next-generation ultra-low-power wireless solutions. Located at booth #52039 in the Venetian Expo, Nordic will present its chip-to-cloud wireless strategy centered on the nRF54L Series ultra-low-power SoCs, alongside Bluetooth LE, cellular IoT, non-terrestrial networks (NTN), Wi-Fi, power management, and cloud lifecycle services.

Nordic also plans to demonstrate market adoption of the nRF54L Series, Matter-enabled smart home solutions, global cellular and satellite connectivity, low-latency Wi-Fi audio streaming, power management ICs, and device management and observability technologies powered by nRF Cloud.
